newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares fall in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares fall in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell back on Sunday in quiet trading dominated by block trades in a rarely-traded gas heating company, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index slipped 0.09 percent to 153.22 points in turnover worth 1.26 million dinars ($1.78 million).
Private transactions of shares in heating manufacturer Aladin Company worth 637,000 dinars accounted for over half of Sunday's business. The share fell 0.21 dinars to 3.99 dinars.
"It looks like a major shareholder is trying to sell his holding," said one brokers. The company is capitalised on the Amman stock exchange at just four million dinars, he said.

Jordan Hotels and Tourism, which closed unchanged on 8.25 dinars, was the second most heavily traded share in terms of value, but its 124,000 dinar turnover was all accounted for in a single transaction.
Middle East Investment Bank and Arab Paper Converting and Trading both traded around 70,000 dinars worth of shares but closed little changed at 1.14 and 1.18 dinars respectively.
Overall falling shares outnumbered rising shares by 16 to 15, with another 15 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.01 percent to 82.34 points.
